d: Ogre Warlord trophy. +8% Defence and +5% max HP.
Emberwyrm trophy. +7% melee damage and +3% crit.
Crudely cured goblin leather. Tougher than raw hide — alchemists cure it further, cooks wrap provisions in it.
A pitted shortsword salvaged from a fallen goblin. Too pitted to reforge. The scrap merchants still pay.
A brute-forged chopping blade, heavy and unbalanced. No smith would waste a forge on it. It sells for its weight.
A curved slab of bone, dense as cured leather. Alchemists and cooks both find a use for it.
Silver-tipped fur from a frost-bound pelt. Cold to the touch, even in summer. Alchemists and cooks both want it.
A yellowed tusk longer than a dagger, wrenched from a brute jaw.
Sludge-thick ichor that knits flesh back together. Alchemists prize its regenerative kick.
The flame-sac of a drake, sloshing with volatile fire. Alchemists handle it with tongs.
A nugget of hell-rock that smoulders without fuel. Alchemists chip it into volatile powders.
An ingot of moltensteel drawn glowing from the Emberforge. Still warm to the touch. The T8 smithing metal — forge it into Moltensteel gear.
Fireproof cloth woven from the ash of the forge-thralls, threaded with living embers. A T8 leathercrafting hide.
A rune-scored fragment of the anvil itself, humming with trapped heat. A rare T8 reagent.
An ingot of null-forged metal, cold as the space between stars. The T9 smithing metal — forge it into Voidsteel gear.
Cloth spun from unravelled rift-thread; it drinks the light that touches it. A T9 leathercrafting hide.
A splinter of a sealed rift, still humming with the void it once opened. A rare T9 reagent.
A shard of the Dawnbroken God's cooling blood — warm to the touch and faintly singing. The signature relic of The Empyrean Throne; a future Dawnsteel
Someone's wages, lost in the shallows a long time ago and grown over twice since. Sells for a pittance. Counts toward the relic set all the same.
Cut from the ninth ship to die on Widow's Wrack. It rings a half-beat before bad weather, which the crew find useful and deeply unpleasant.
Salt-swollen and still legible. It predicts the great ebb to the hour, in a hand nobody at the Admiralty recognises.
Broader than a shield and lighter than paper. Nothing marks it — not fire, not starsteel, not the void. It was shed, not taken.
Recovered from an island that is on no chart. It has never guttered. Crews who carry it report arriving where they meant to, which is not always welco
Scratched into a hatch cover by someone who did not survive the writing. It marks Gravekeel Spit, and the words around the edge are not directions.
Drawn on the back of a warrant, in the hand of the man it was issued for. Corsair's Gibbet is circled twice.
Vellum that has been underwater for centuries and has not softened. It shows a city, and the city has streets.
Not a map of a place — a map of a depth. The soundings run past the edge of the parchment and keep going in the margin.
Ship-iron that has spent forty years in seawater and come out harder than it went in. No forge on land can reproduce it, and every shipwright in Ember
Light as ash, stiff as starsteel, and it does not rot. Hulls ribbed with it have come home from water that took everything else.
A knot of stone and metal the deep water grew around something it swallowed. Warm on one side. The yard will not say which hull it goes into until it
Cut from a wreck on The Wracks. Still rifled, still true, and somebody else's initials are stamped into the breech. The yard files them off.
Followed the ship home from water that had no business holding birds. It sleeps in the rigging and screams before weather. +5% treasure find.
Given at Emberwatch to the handful who have sailed everything there is to sail. Salt-stiff, and the hem has been repaired more than once. +5% Sailing
Ship-scrap crusted an inch thick in shell. Chip it clean and it still smelts.
Somebody's bottle, forty years of surf ago. Frosted soft and edgeless. Cuts into cheap, pretty things.
Cut from the Warren, where the forest is underneath you. Steeps into a serviceable low reagent.
Hull planking off a ship that died on the reef. Salt-hardened past anything a living tree gives you.
Still supple, still black, still smells of the pitch pot. Rigging wants nothing else.
Dry kegs out of a dead magazine. Whoever sealed them knew their trade and did not survive it.
Split down one side, so it sounds wrong — but bell bronze is bell bronze, and no mine on the coast yields it.
A cargo manifest, legible and stamped. The Admiralty pays a bounty for these and does not explain why.
It refracts wrong — the light comes out at an angle it did not go in at. Jewellers pay well and work fast.
Grows where no light reaches, which should not be possible. Alchemists have stopped asking.
Dressed masonry from a tower sixty feet under. Someone cut these blocks in air.
Palm-sized, and warm. It sits between drake and wraith on any tanner's bench.
Struck by a mint that no longer exists, for a country that no longer exists. The metal alone is worth a house.
Timber from trees that grow below the waterline in the Trench. Darker than shadowwood and it does not float.
Broad as a shield, light as paper. Shed, not taken — nothing alive is peeling these off.
Something came down out of the sky into deep water a very long time ago, and it is still warm.
One piece of a circlet that was worn by whatever the Sunken Crown was built for. There are others down there.
